name: AppDynamics
tools: Browser Synthetic Monitoring and Private Synthetic Agent

beginner.summary: For developers, support engineers, SREs and operations staff who are new to Cisco AppDynamics, now sold and documented as Splunk AppDynamics after Cisco acquired Splunk. Covers the Controller and agent architecture on SaaS and on-premises, the application, tier and node model, installing the Java, .NET, Node.js, Python and Machine Agents, business transaction discovery, flow maps, the Metric Browser, snapshots and call graphs, errors, baselines, health rules, policies and actions, custom dashboards, browser real user monitoring, agent troubleshooting, and a three-tier instrumentation capstone.
prerequisites: Can deploy and run a simple web application written in Java, .NET, Node.js or Python on Linux or Windows
Understands HTTP requests, response codes, SQL databases and basic latency concepts such as averages and percentiles
Has a lab Controller (a SaaS trial tenant or an on-premises demo Controller) with an access key and a Linux VM or laptop where agents can be installed
outcomes: Install and register Java, .NET, Node.js, Python and Machine Agents with correct application, tier and node names
Read flow maps, business transaction metrics, snapshots and call graphs to locate a slow method or backend
Create health rules on baselines and wire them to policies that send email and HTTP request actions
Build a custom dashboard and enable browser real user monitoring for a monitored web application

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already run AppDynamics agents and read flow maps, snapshots and health rules, and now need to tune and extend a deployment.
